page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal is a bare-metal server instance featuring 288 vCPUs mapped to 144 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor. Operating at a base frequency of 4.2 GHz, this x86_64 architecture includes a 504 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 2232 GB of DDR5 memory running at 6 GHz, yielding approximately 7.75 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided locally via six NVMe SSDs totaling 16242 GB, while no dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core CPU scores and Passmark CPU scores ranking in the top 10% of tested systems. Memory subsystem throughput is exceptionally high, with read-only small block cached bandwidth reaching 23041.86 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds at 412.25 GB/sec. The server demonstrates strong database and transactional capabilities, achieving 422.06 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and top-tier results in Passmark database operations. However, a notable performance tradeoff is observed in LLM text generation, where the system registers average to poor speeds, such as 41.9 tokens per second for a small 135M model, despite strong prompt processing capabilities.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c4-highmem-288-lssd-metal delivers high resource density by combining massive memory capacity with high-speed local NVMe storage on a single bare-metal node. This consolidation reduces the overhead associated with distributed network storage and virtualized hypervisors. The hardware profile is optimized for memory-intensive and storage-heavy workloads, including large-scale relational databases, in-memory data stores like Redis, high-throughput static web serving, and complex multi-threaded data processing tasks.

Lacking a GPU, this x86_64 system relies on its high-frequency CPU cores and massive memory bandwidth, which benchmarks place in the top 10% for multi-core processing and database operations. While prompt processing for medium LLMs is strong, text generation speeds remain a bottleneck. The server offers high resource density, making it qualitatively cost-effective for consolidating large-scale in-memory databases, high-throughput web serving, and intensive data-processing workloads that require direct access to physical hardware and low-latency local storage.
